summary.oneLiner: Q1 revenue missed due to project delays in Bharat Net and battery upgrades, but order book surged to ₹1,500+ crores with EV charging momentum accelerating; Hyderabad plant commissioning in Oct 2025 will unlock scale and margin expansion, while Tritium's TRI-FLEX and lifetime warranty signal long-term global potential.

one-line thesis: Q1 revenue missed due to project delays in Bharat Net and battery upgrades, but order book surged to ₹1,500+ crores with EV charging momentum accelerating; Hyderabad plant commissioning in Oct 2025 will unlock scale and margin expansion, while Tritium's TRI-FLEX and lifetime warranty signal long-term global potential.
financial scorecard: Revenue: -38% YoY (standalone), -19% YoY (consolidated); EBITDA/margin: +8.6% margin (standalone), -38.6cr EBITDA (consolidated); PAT (rptd): +1.1cr (standalone), -71cr (consolidated); PAT (normalized): +1.1cr (standalone), -62cr (consolidated); Order book: ₹1,500+ crores (₹1,200+ crores hardware); Net debt: Reduced to 0.35x debt-equity post-rights issue (from 0.7x), ₹108cr IPO cash remaining
guidance: Revenue growth: 50% YoY standalone; EBITDA: 2.5x improvement; Order inflow: Sustained by ₹1,500cr backlog; Capex/commissioning: Hyderabad plant SOP in Oct 2025, full ramp-up by Q4FY26
order book & pipeline: ₹1,500+ crores total (₹1,200+ crores hardware), including large lithium-ion battery upgrades, Middle East/Africa exports, and EV charger framework agreements in Southeast Asia
segment / subsidiary detail: Critical Power: ₹98cr revenue (standalone), down due to Bharat Net/delays; 70% market share in rural telecom battery upgrades; 30% revenue from Africa/SE Asia; EV Chargers: ₹53cr standalone (61% QoQ growth), 50% AC/50% DC mix; Harmony Gen 2 adopted by 6 of top 10 customers; Tritium: $8M Q1 bookings, TRI-FLEX pipeline building, lifetime warranty on power modules launched
growth verticals / optionality: Global EV charging framework with Southeast Asia clean energy player; entry into electric trucking segment; DC microgrid-integrated charging solutions under development; potential Tritium product localization in India
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improved to 32.7% (standalone) due to richer EV product mix and cost optimization; Harmony Gen 2 delivered higher value with margin expansion; Tritium's high fixed costs drag consolidated margins; Hyderabad plant to reduce per-unit cost by 15-20% at full capacity
capex / expansion: ₹35cr spent in Q1 on Hyderabad plant; total capex from IPO proceeds: ₹292cr (₹257cr + ₹35cr); remaining ₹108cr to be fully utilized by Sep 2025 for plant commissioning and working capital
capital allocation: Rights issue ₹260cr allocated: ₹55cr debt repayment, ₹107cr promoter loan conversion, ₹85cr Tritium support, ₹12cr corporate purposes; IPO funds prioritized for Hyderabad plant (₹292cr), working capital, and R&D; no dividend or buyback planned
risks & watch-items: Tritium turnaround slower than expected; geopolitical supply chain delays for rare earth components (minor impact); EV price wars compressing margins; project execution delays due to monsoon/approvals; consolidation risk from smaller competitors
management quality / tone: Confident and transparent; acknowledged Q1 miss but emphasized strong order book and pipeline; highlighted operational discipline, product innovation, and long-term strategic bets; tone focused on execution and FY26 guidance adherence
non-obvious takeaways: Exicom is the only Indian EV charger maker designing its own controller (CPU) in-house — a deep tech differentiator; Tritium's lifetime warranty on power modules is a global first, signaling confidence in reliability and a potential industry standard setter
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tritium's prolonged losses and delayed turnaround | Servotech Power Systems | loser | Low | Servotech's growth is in solar/EPC; Exicom's scale, global reach, and integrated manufacturing give it structural advantage in pure-play EV charging |
| Lack of domestic manufacturing scale in EV charging | OEMs (Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai) | beneficiary | High | Exicom's Hyderabad plant and Gen 2 product will become preferred supplier for premium EV makers seeking reliable, high-margin charging infrastructure |

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as a "Leading player for Energy Storage Systems & Power Management Systems" with a strong customer base including telecom and data centers, and projects deployed across India, Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, Nigeria, etc.
- In Electric Mobility it claims to be "India's one of the Top EV charger company", with customers among major CPOs, OEMs and fleets and a product range spanning 3.3 kW to 600 kW output including distributed and BESS solutions.
- Critical Power strategy is framed around "Five forces redefining how operators buy site power": higher-density 5G loads, lead-acid to intelligent lithium, generator to hybrid energy, backup to active energy asset, and alarms to fleet intelligence.
- Positions on lifetime outcomes rather than price: "Operators increasingly evaluate site power through lifetime outcomes and Exicom's end to end product stack allows for low risk adjusted lifetime cost per network hour"; in Govt supplies the deck claims "Exicom has 60% market share of this project".
- Tritium is positioned around strategic customers: TRI-FLEX/DCFlex under field and lab validation by "one of the largest open public charging network and fleet company in the US", and the first GRID-FLEX system delivered to a hyperscale customer and operating since June.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Tritium] The overseas fast-charging arm remains loss-making at the consolidated level but shows momentum — Q1 bookings of USD 20.8m, described by the CEO as "~2x QoQ", with a stated "second consecutive quarter ~10Mn$ sales".
- [Regulation - Haryana] Building code notified 5-Jun-26 mandates 1:3 charge points per car park for commercial buildings and 1:5 for group housing/RWA, with 100% EV-ready conduits, basement and stilt charging allowed and EV infrastructure exempt from FAR.
- [Regulation - Delhi] Delhi EV Policy 2026 notified 30-Jun-26 with a ₹15,000 Cr four-year outlay, 30,000+ charging points planned, one charging station per OEM dealer, e-3W and e-N1 only from Jan-27, and e-2W subsidy up to ₹30,000.
- [Regulation - PM E-Drive] ₹504 Cr sanctioned in this tranche (~25% of the ₹2,000 Cr charging pool) for 4,874 public chargers, Karnataka largest at 1,243; the deck's own read is that this is "a positive for Industry. Not a very high target market for Exicom".
- [Plant transition] Manufacturing is mid-shift from Gurgaon to Hyderabad, with both plants running in parallel during the transition.
